originalFinding.title: Disclosed secret exposure without a recorded rotation/revocation decision
originalFinding.location: Parent tool transcripts (07:15 marker reload; MEMORY-LAB-002 prose filter); HANDOFF.md line 37
originalFinding.evidence: Disclosed by the parent: the marker API key was rendered once through an incomplete regex redaction, and Tailscale credential identifiers from MEMORY-LAB-002 were rendered through an insufficient prose filter. Marker metadata shows a server restart at 2026-10-08T09:13:49-05:00, and the marker text says keys rotate on restart (inference: the 07:15 key is no longer valid; not verified). MEMORY-LAB-002 records that an earlier Tailscale key was revoked after transcript exposure. No revocation or rotation decision is recorded for the exposed identifiers.
originalFinding.remediation: Ask the operator whether to revoke/replace the exposed Tailscale auth key, following the earlier precedent, and confirm workspace API key rotation through the normal Nuke-managed service restart if any doubt remains. Keep literal-value redaction of every parsed secret plus identifier patterns (auth key ..., Key ... was revoked, k...CNTRL, tskey-...) before any rendering.

parentDisposition: Bounded local evidence distinguishes memory keyId from full authKey. Historical API key is redacted in retained output, so revocation unverified. Operator disposition requested and pending. No credentials/services/provider queries changed.

originalFinding.title: Gate runtime claims native diagnostics on stdout, but every gate stdout log is empty
originalFinding.location: gate-runtime/gate-observer.c lines 2-3; gate-runtime/README.md lines 38-39; gate-runtime/*/stdout.log (7 files, 0 bytes)
originalFinding.evidence: Clock runs with the same stock arguments and normal exit retained 2348 to 1791119 bytes of native stdout. The gate adapter ends nonzero runs with _Exit(status), which does not flush stdio buffers (inference for the cause). As a result, no native log (ROM loading, CPU reset lines) is retained for the seven gate probes.
originalFinding.remediation: Flush stdout (fflush(NULL)) before _Exit, or make stdout unbuffered, in the diagnostic adapter. Correct the README and the adapter comment to say native stdout was not captured. Rerun only if native log evidence is needed.

parentDisposition: README and C header corrected to disclose seven empty stdout files; executable/body unchanged. Native stdout retention and real buffering behavior remain open. No claim that documentation repairs lost logs.

originalFinding.title: Clock reversal note omits the correlating native reset log
originalFinding.evidence: In all three wrapped runs, "Main CPU:  RESET." is logged between the first 7,8 pair and the second 7,8 pair (reviewer extraction: reset log at record index 2). Correlation is not causal proof, and the README statement is not false.
originalFinding.remediation: Cite the interleaved native reset line as correlated evidence while keeping the cause unproven unless a reset event is observed directly.

parentDisposition: Clock README now cites native RESET line between initial clock pairs in all three logs, explicitly correlation only. No causal or reset-event proof claimed.

originalFinding.title: Lifecycle transcript lacks a single-fault control for receipt acceptance after a changed postflight
originalFinding.evidence: For (preflight true, postflight false), mutation 2 combines "run before preflight" with an inverted receipt, so the ordering assertion fails first. The receipt-value check (line 60) and the postflight-argument check (line 59) are never independently proven to reject a wrongly accepted receipt in that case. The receipt check is proven only for rejected preflight (Preflight(false), Receipt(true)). Decision-level coverage of post-inventory change exists in IdentityAndInventory.
originalFinding.remediation: Add single-fault controls: correct order with Receipt(true) after Postflight(false), and correct order with a wrong Postflight argument.

parentDisposition: Four independent lifecycle controls added, including changed-postflight receipt acceptance and postflight-argument faults. Full current oracle87/87 passes. Requires reviewer revalidation.

originalFinding.title: Receipt contract accepts a vacuous zero-test receipt
originalFinding.evidence: Every count scenario has at least one nonzero count. No scenario rejects Passed=0, Failed=0, Skipped=0, Aborted=0, which would let an empty run satisfy "zero-failure/zero-skip for the claimed scope" (TR-VICE-ORACLE-001 AC4, TEST-VICE-001 AC3).
originalFinding.remediation: Add a no-tests-executed rejection scenario with a wrong-acceptance control. Optionally bind the expected executed count to the claimed scope.

parentDisposition: Zero-executed receipt rejection case and wrong-acceptance control added. Full current oracle87/87 passes. Expected scope denominator beyond current contract not silently claimed.

originalFinding.title: Phase 1 fixtures are not yet reusable by real adapters without refactoring; boundary contract takes ResolvedPath as input
originalFinding.evidence: ProveDecision always constructs an NSubstitute probe, and fixtures live inline in [InlineData]/switch blocks. Unlike the Phase 2 suites, no provider seam binds a real adapter to the same rows. The wrapper-boundary DTO supplies ResolvedPath, so it cannot detect an adapter that mis-resolves traversal or links.
originalFinding.remediation: Before production adapters, extract fixture rows to shared MemberData and add a provider seam. Require the real boundary binding to compute ResolvedPath from RequestedPath against real filesystem fixtures (junctions, .., case variants).

parentDisposition: Shared MemberData/fixture builders and supplied-provider assertions added. Boundary requested input no longer supplies resolved path; result path independently asserted with wrong-path controls. Actual filesystem/junction resolver unimplemented and unproven. Names,rows and assertions preserved; current oracle87/87.
